{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=Falcon
#   --gres=gpu:2
#   --ntasks-per-node=2
#   --nodes=1
#   --hint=nomultithread
#   --time=20:00:00
#   --qos=qos_gpu-t3
#   --cpus-per-task=8
#   -C a100

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 2 \
  -c 8 \
  --gpus=2 \
  --time=20h \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --qos=qos_gpu-t3 has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: QoS-related limits/priority/preemption behavior may not be applied, changing queue time
# or job survivability.

# NOTE: Slurm constraint -C a100 (GPU/feature constraint) has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: you may be scheduled on non-A100 GPUs, affecting performance/compatibility.

# NOTE: Slurm --hint=nomultithread has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: if SMT/hyperthreading is enabled, you may see different CPU binding and performance.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=Falcon is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module purge
module load cpuarch/amd
module load anaconda-py3/2023.03
conda activate claire

set -x

MODEL=tiiuae/falcon-7b
OUTDIR=$WORK/../commun/Claire/pretrain/Claire-7B-0.1_1
mkdir -p $OUTDIR

# Slurm used srun with --output/--error. Approximate by redirecting stdout/stderr.
exec >"$OUTDIR/training_log.out" 2>&1

# Run inside the allocation.
python pretrain.py \
--devices 2 \
--num_nodes 1 \
--data_dir "$SCRATCH/../commun/preprocessed_data/Claire/lit-gpt/padded_8_grouped/$MODEL" \
--checkpoint_dir "$WORK/../commun/Claire/checkpoints/$MODEL" \
--language fr \
--out_dir "$OUTDIR" \
--precision bf16-true \
--num_epochs 1000 \
--max_checkpoints 39 \
--enable_validation true \
--save_interval 1800 \
--eval_interval 1800 \
--early_stopping 4 \
--lora_r 16 \
--lora_alpha 32
'
"
}
